items.title: Add shared-world physics simulation and authenticated consequences
items.description:
## Goal
Add authoritative, recoverable physics simulation for a shared world while keeping domain state, policy, actions, authorization and meaningful consequences in Prolog. Treat native physics as transient world state, not a second domain engine.

## Delivery
1. Define world-local physical bodies, colliders, joints/attachments, authority, epoch, incarnation and structural revision in ontology-owned state. Visual Eidolons and physical shapes are separate; a GLB's triangles or declared visual bounds do not silently become collision authority.
2. Install one retained simulation owner for each active simulated world through the existing runtime/resource lifecycle. It consumes committed desired state, steps Rapier through audited Rustler NIF calls, and publishes current epoch/tick body poses. Physics is optional and enabled by committed Prolog policy, not inferred from whether a scene looks static; a nonphysical world starts no simulator. Respect bounded native work, BEAM scheduler safety, reader/writer locking and native failure retirement; reuse existing owners and notifications.
3. Compose parent/local scene transforms with body motion under a single pose source per occurrence. Bind frames to stable entity/body identity plus authority epoch, simulation incarnation, structural revision and tick. Reconnect and sequence gaps rebuild from current state; stale frames and deleted/recreated entities cannot resurrect or move an object.
4. Filter motion frames and perception candidates through each agent's current authorized view. Keep visual/perception bounds separate from collision bounds. Measure whether existing Rapier/Parry queries suffice before adding another spatial index; any index is a derived projection of the world owner, never a second knowledge base.
5. Admit bounded, quantized contact/obstruction observations from an authenticated physics producer through the existing reaction/action/atomic transaction path. Prolog decides their meaning and durable effects. Current sealing rejects a write proof that reads a live native query; do not add a functor exemption or classify live physics as proof-bound. Bind observations to world/authority incarnation, entity/body revision and tick, reject stale/duplicate reports, and preserve owner recovery without replaying old reactions.

## Acceptance
- A chair can be pushed without a label/material refresh snapping it back; a structural edit or authority restart invalidates old frames.
- A hinged door can be obstructed: physics reports the observation, Prolog decides and atomically commits the domain consequence. An in-proof live physics query is rejected.
- A held object follows its holder and survives attach/drop, deletion, reconnect and current-authority recovery according to an explicit checkpoint policy.
- Unauthorized viewers receive neither hidden scene objects nor their motion frames. Collider-less or visually larger objects are not lost from perception selection.
- Native stepping and queries do not block an ontology state owner or ordinary BEAM schedulers; failures retire the affected world visibly. Repeated unchanged checks do not rebuild Prolog/history state or cause disk writes; real updates still apply.

This is separate from static GLB mesh rendering, which can be delivered first without a physics NIF. Direction and caveats: [world overview](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/world.md), [archived client/world direction](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/outdated/client-world-direction.md), [archived consequence direction](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/outdated/world-consequence-direction.md), and [current multiwrite map](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/multiwrite-architecture.md). The archived consequence draft's in-proof `physics_contact/2` path conflicts with current sealing and is not an implementation recipe.

## Delivery boundaries after the ontology/space review
Completed foundations remain [QUD.4](nimbalyst://QUD.4)–[QUD.8](nimbalyst://QUD.8). Remaining normal-world integration is [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27), with governed space vocabulary in [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33); actual-lobby player/Vive acceptance is [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26) and deferred real-lobby blocked/closed door acceptance is [QUD.36](nimbalyst://QUD.36). Keep this umbrella open alongside the existing held-object, authorized query, distinct-impact and multi-viewer tasks.

Ontology and space are independent classes. Reuse the existing subscribed committed-diff path for live collider definitions; do not impose recipe re-adoption or duplicate synchronization on every live edit. No backward-compatibility requirement or parallel old/new engine is introduced. Same lobby identity/history preservation and applicable validator/deployment authority still apply. Text/3D ontology editing is separate work, not a blanket prerequisite for this physics umbrella.

items.title: Expose live routes as Prolog facts beyond root and move host selection policy into Prolog
items.description:
# Goal

Make the live route directory fact "key K currently answers for ontology Y at address A, until lease expiry" available to Prolog policy in every hosted ontology's read-only proofs, then move host selection rules out of Erlang into Prolog and delete the Erlang ordering they replace.

Origin: Yan, 2026-10-07, during the node-enrollment routing review (frozen scope tree-02, session "Directory deployment fix review"). Separate scope from tree-02; do not fold into it.

# What exists today

- `src/predicates/quod_directory_predicates.erl` already defines `directory_host(+Ontology, ?GenesisAnchor, ?NodeKey, ?Host, ?Port)` over the ETS route index (`quod_directory:directory_hosts/1`) and `directory_control_peer(?NodeKey)` over root's committed `peer_admitted/4`. Both are registered as `query` class and are available **only while executing `quod:root`** (the `ctx_ns` check in `directory_host_5/3` and `directory_control_peer_1/3`).
- `quod_directory:directory_hosts/1` returns active public system routes only: rows with status `confirmed`, `Expiry > now`, deterministic key order; private contacts excluded. Rows carry `{Ns, system, RouteKey, NodeKey, {Host,Port}, confirmed, GenesisAnchor, Role, Expiry, Epoch, Sequence}`. The predicate currently drops `Role` and `Expiry`.
- Routes are deliberately soft state: signed, leased node-actor generations installed by `quod_directory`, rebuilt after restart, never written to consensus (module doc of `quod_directory`, `doc/lifecycle-and-routing.md` "Routes and local notifications"). Authority to advertise comes from committed facts (`hosts_ontology/4` discoverable in the node identity, `system_ontology/2` catalogue for system entries); receivers verify those before installing a route. The predicate must stay a projection of that verified index, not a second authority.
- Predicate module loading: `src/quod_app.erl` line 476 lists `[quod_directory_predicates, quod_ontology_predicates]` for root.
- Existing tests for the predicate and its live-bridge handling: `test/quod_committed_projection_tests.erl` (lines ~255, 262, 305) and `test/quod_dtx_tests.erl` (lines ~640-660, 916: sealing a plan that depended on `directory_host/5` must fail with `non_transactional_dependency`).

# Erlang selection code that would become Prolog policy

- `src/predicates/quod_ask.erl`: `open_directory_scope/1`, `choose_directory_scope/2`, `open_anchored_routes/2`, `eligible_routes/1`, `verified_plain_read_routes/3` (which confirmed validator routes an ask uses, anchor-conflict handling, local-vs-remote preference).
- `src/quod_foreign_log.erl`: `current_route_candidates/2`, `current_peer_endpoints/7`, `history_source_candidates/1`, `directory_route_hints/2` (endpoint preference order: request contact, live, certified historical, third-party supplied; capped at two per peer).
- Candidate future users: enrollment custodian choice in `priv/ontologies/quod_node.pl`, availability rules (how many confirmed hosts make an ontology available), discovery ACL (who may be told about a route).

# Hard constraints (from AGENTS.md and quod_predicates)

1. **Determinism.** A live ETS fact differs between nodes. It may be read in read-only and local proofs only. `quod_predicates` already records `live_observation` bridge use at dispatch and `quod_dtx` refuses to seal a plan that depended on one (`record_bridge_use/4`, `allowed/2`: "query reads everywhere except a deterministic policy verdict"). Keep the `query` class and the live-observation dependency marker when widening; add tests that a committed diff or atomic plan depending on the widened predicate still fails to seal.
2. **No second domain engine.** The predicate stays a read-only bridge over the directory's existing index. No copying of routes into any ontology, no new process, no cache.
3. **Replace, do not duplicate.** When a selection rule moves to Prolog, delete the Erlang ordering it replaces in the same scope and report the line delta. No parallel old/new path.
4. **Not transport.** Dissemination of routes (who pushes signed pages to whom) stays in `quod_directory_control`; this ticket does not touch it.
5. **Private contacts stay excluded** from the public fact; a private-route predicate, if ever needed, is a separate decision with its own ACL.
6. No format, wire or ledger change. No deployment authority implied.

# Proposed shape

- Widen `directory_host/5` to any hosted ontology's read-only proof context (drop the `quod:root` gate, keep `query` class). Decide whether to extend arity to expose `Role` (`validator`/`observer`) and lease `Expiry`, since host selection needs role and liveness. Suggest `directory_host/7` or a second predicate `directory_route(Ontology, Anchor, NodeKey, Host, Port, Role, ExpiresAt)`; pick one, do not keep both.
- Keep `directory_control_peer/1` root-only (it projects root membership).
- Resolve governed bridge availability before widening the context gate. Trace retained founding manifests, ordinary lifecycle/composition and compatible validator deployment; changing quod_app.erl's package module list cannot grant an existing ontology a new external-predicate capability. Do not load a bridge globally as an implicit authorization bypass. Demonstrate non-root use in a scope actually authorized to use that bridge; a demonstrated missing capability must pass the applicable architecture gate, not be hidden behind a module-file edit.
- Write the first consumer: host selection for asks in Prolog (which confirmed validator to prefer, local-first rule, anchor-conflict refusal), called from `quod_ask` through the existing predicate seam; then remove the Erlang ordering above.
- Second consumer, optional: foreign-log endpoint preference order.

# Acceptance

- `directory_host` (or its successor) proves in a read-only proof of a non-root ontology and returns exactly the active, confirmed, public rows for that namespace in deterministic order; expired and private rows absent.
- Sealing any nonempty diff or atomic plan that read the predicate fails with the existing `non_transactional_dependency` error (extend `quod_dtx_tests`).
- Ask host selection behaviour unchanged for existing CT (`quod_ask_SUITE`), with the Erlang selection code deleted and the delta reported.
- Docs: update `quod_directory_predicates` moduledoc, `doc/lifecycle-and-routing.md` "Routes and local notifications", and `doc/runtime-and-agents.md` if predicate classes are listed there.
- Standing gates (clean sequential, true exits, frozen tree) before commit; separate label bump.

# Out of scope

- Self-network-pull transport cause (documented separately in the enrollment routing evidence).
- Directory dissemination topology (fixed in tree-02).
- Making routes consensus facts: rejected, addresses churn on every reschedule and leases expire without a transaction.

## Cross-check with governed-world work
[QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27) must resolve the same immutable founding-capability invariant; neither ticket approves the removed mutable-module experiment. Sharing that architectural constraint is not a reason to merge routing policy with physics or block either on an unrelated client feature. There is no backward-compatibility requirement: replace the old predicate/selection path, while preserving proofs, current identity/history and the applicable release authority. If the selected implementation cannot satisfy the no-format-change boundary above, stop at that concrete architecture decision rather than silently expanding scope.

items.title: Build the general Quod GUI framework for VR and desktop
items.description:
Implement the general ontology-based GUI framework described in the [GUI plan](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/gui-plan.md). The plan is the design source of truth; proposed APIs still need implementation-level specification.

References:
- [Interactive visual concept](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/gui-concept.mockup.html)
- [Claude Fable review](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/evidence/gui-plan-review-3/fable-review.md)
- [Independent assessment and disposition](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/evidence/gui-plan-review-3/assessment.md)

Agreed requirements:
- Reusable GUI component classes instantiated through existing ontology semantics, usable by arbitrary components and applications, including non-lobby examples.
- Common controls in the first milestone: text inputs, buttons, selections, sliders, rotary knobs and composed forms.
- Convenient Prolog authoring and submitted field bindings. Domain actions follow ontology events and authorized react_on handlers; shared GUI behavior supplies registration and correlation without manual per-widget reactions.
- Resolve the intended human through authenticated context or authorized question state. Opening fails in Prolog when there is no connected human receiver or no authorized responsible agent able to handle the interaction. This requirement is settled.
- Accepted questions may remain in the HUD until the human chooses to answer. No proof remains suspended during editing, and opening does not guarantee continued connection until an answer.
- Shared ontology state owns question identity, status, cancellation and accepted answers; drafts stay local. Preserve existing transaction, authority, recovery and exact-outcome guarantees.
- Reuse Eidolons, marks, existing client controllers, actions, reactions and agent-work owners. No parallel GUI domain engine or shadow queue.
- VR-first ergonomics, moderate adjustable panel translucency with opaque readable controls/text, accessible input alternatives and desktop operation.

Delivery checklist:
- [ ] Specify the executable form/component API and trace human/agent binding and presentation through existing owners. Resolve the live-observation/material-write integration internally without reopening the settled failure behavior or hiding partial writes.
- [ ] Implement shared GUI ontology classes, composition, field/event binding and automatic authorized reaction behavior.
- [ ] Implement authenticated presentation, HUD discovery and shared question lifecycle, including concurrent openings, stale revisions, duplicate responses, cancellation, disconnects and uncertain operation outcomes.
- [ ] Extend the existing representation/controller path and deliver the common control suite with the agreed visual treatment.
- [ ] Demonstrate an elaborate form both in the lobby and on an independent application component.
- [ ] Verify behavior through production seams, including absence/refusal, event authority, agent loss, atomic question transitions and unchanged repeated-operation cost.
- [ ] Validate VR legibility, reach, target selection, keyboard entry, transparency and comfort on intended hardware; desktop mockup checks do not establish headset ergonomics.

Read AGENTS.md and the relevant architecture/proof/multiwrite specifications before implementation. Review advice is consultative: use the independent assessment, including its rejected recommendations.

## Relationship to ontology editing and optional physics
The GUI plan governs this common component/question-lifecycle scope. The later ontology/space decisions refine representation integration: [QUD.32](nimbalyst://QUD.32) unifies ordinary ontology-instance Eidolons and ACL reflection, [QUD.34](nimbalyst://QUD.34) supplies the dedicated highlighted text editor, and [QUD.35](nimbalyst://QUD.35) supplies the 3D ontology-editing application. Reuse controls and existing lenses/encodings/marks across these consumers; do not build duplicate editors or presentation engines.

An ontology can have several views of one authoritative content/history without becoming a space; containment/optional physical-space semantics are [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33). General GUI work must function in nonphysical contexts. These application tickets need not wait for this entire broad GUI milestone if existing controls suffice. No backward-compatibility shims; replace superseded dispatch paths. Keep the settled absent-human/agent failure behavior and all original lifecycle/hardware acceptance above.

comments.body:
Planning artifact: [Collision aware player movement plan](doc/player-movement-plan.md). Traced the camera/XR path, signed simulation view, Prolog selection, retained physics owner and pinned Rapier controller. The plan covers capsule movement, moving-door contact, spawn/teleport validation, control authorization, shared query mechanics for prediction, fencing/recovery, future non-cubic terrain and production-owner cost checks.

Yan selected teleportation, snap turning and smooth controller travel. Primary hardware target: original HTC Vive; retain portable Babylon/WebXR input discovery and configurable touchpad/thumbstick bindings. Actual host OS/runtime/browser qualification and physical hardware tests remain required.

Status remains in-progress. Planning only: one documentation file added, no production implementation or runtime tests performed. Local documentation links and whitespace checked. The requested Conceptual Thinking server is unavailable in this session; available Sequential Thinking was used.

Corrected the planning basis following Yan's objection: the human-user instance can bind to different agents with arbitrary physical forms. The original universal capsule/upright walking/head-to-body assumptions were wrong and have been removed from doc/player-movement-plan.md.

Traced the shared human/agent vocabularies, signup and human instance template, signed principal admission, client agent selection, world/Eidolon identity model and physical body/group revisions. Archived client-world-direction §4.3 explicitly separates acting identity, controlled character and appearance. Current shipped code supplies generic signed agent selection, but the inspected templates/client paths do not implement a general played-agent physical control binding; local selection must not be mistaken for authorization or impersonation.

The revised plan starts with that domain relation and representative differently shaped agents before choosing native operations. It requires rotation/compound clearance and embodiment-specific VR mappings. Browser WASM prediction is no longer a settled architecture choice. No production code changed. Planning remains in progress; no implementation-ready or completion claim.

Implementation is in the working tree, following Quod's Prolog → governed Erlang external predicate → retained physics owner interface. BBSvx's predicate/effect pattern was inspected. Human principal, controlled agent, physical body and authored camera position/orientation are distinct; there is no universal capsule. Added explicit hull/compound bodies and fixed triangle surfaces for non-cubic terrain, swept movement/rotation, supported teleport, occupancy-tested live reposition, registration/revision fencing and desktop/XR adapters.

Yan's requested Claude consultation used Fable. Findings and independently verified resolutions: [review](doc/evidence/player-movement/review-04-implementation.md), [evidence and hardware checklist](doc/evidence/player-movement/README.md). Final targeted owner suite: 119 passed; proof/lifecycle regression: 308 passed; native geometry/motion: 16 passed. Client tests, TypeScript, isolated bundle and WebGL rendering smoke passed. Tests include door obstruction and escape query, occupied landing, mid-air world revision, wedge settlement, moved/deleted support, authorization/reconnect/deadlines and unchanged-operation cost.

Status remains in-progress: original HTC Vive hardware acceptance is NOT performed. The available browser reports immersive-vr unsupported. Hardware checklist is recorded; no desktop or simulated-camera result is being represented as Vive validation. Changes are uncommitted, and no deployment or ontology-history migration was performed.

Official Chrome for Testing 157.0.8091.0 software preflight executed on Linux/RTX 4090, sandbox enabled, private Monado simulated HMD. Headset discovery and immersive support succeed; session creation fails before rendering. Native tracing identifies NVIDIA ICD load denied by Chromium's XR sandbox, then VK_ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER. Two process-local preload diagnostics also failed; no security flags were disabled. All test runtimes exited cleanly. Evidence: doc/evidence/player-movement/linux-webxr-20261008/README.md and chrome-preflight-01..05. SteamVR is not installed and was not exercised. Physical Vive acceptance remains outstanding; task stays in progress.

Linux native WebXR software preflight now passes on RTX 4090 using the private Chromium 157.0.8091.0 build, with its browser/XR sandbox enabled. Investigation identified NVIDIA lazy EGL/backend/compiler loads missing from the existing XR prewarm closure, plus GLVND manifest directory enumeration. A local 28-line upstream XR-hook patch resolves it; the final incremental build took 6.923 seconds. Both traced and untraced preflights passed two immersive sessions with 120 stereo frames each, local-floor, changing native tracked poses and both simulated controllers; browser/runtime exits were 0. The fixture and its assertions were unchanged.

Exact patch, hashes, retained failures and successful evidence: [October 9 investigation](doc/evidence/player-movement/linux-webxr-20261009/README.md). No Quod production source, global OpenXR setting, ordinary browser profile or system package changed. This is a simulated native browser/runtime/GPU result; original Vive display/tracking/controller mappings and Quod collision locomotion on physical hardware remain untested. Status stays in-progress; this is not hardware acceptance or ticket completion.

Vive hardware prerequisite check: SteamVR is installed and its Lighthouse driver has no unresolved linked libraries. HDMI EDID identifies the HTC Vive, but Linux rejected its USB hub (0bb4:2210, path 1-3) with error -28 / “Not enough bandwidth”, leaving it unconfigured with no tracking/receiver devices. No physical XR runtime was started. Waiting for a different direct PC USB port to check enumeration. Evidence retained in doc/evidence/player-movement/linux-webxr-20261009/vive-usb-01; Quod production sources unchanged. Hardware acceptance remains open.

Physical Vive/WebXR prerequisite now demonstrated. USB port change restored all headset/receiver devices. Two exact upstream Monado SteamVR compatibility fixes (4156456d, cfa6078b) and a temporary Vive-only Hyprland monitor exception enabled Wayland display leasing. No Quod production source or persistent desktop configuration changes. `vive-webxr-02` passes two real immersive sessions with 120 stereo frames each, changing head poses, local-floor and both htc-vive controller profiles; browser/runtime exit 0, sandbox enabled. Yan confirmed visible colored output in a longer repeat. That repeat's first session completes 1,800 frames, but cycle 2 fails on missing viewer pose; Yan reports removing the headset during the test. The longer run remains recorded as failed, not a two-session pass. Original simulated regression after runtime corrections also passes. Evidence: doc/evidence/player-movement/linux-webxr-20261009/vive-hardware.md. Quod movement/controller/haptics and full Vive hardware acceptance remain open; item stays in progress.

Yan requires acceptance in the actual current lobby/runtime, without a substitute test world. The unused disposable launcher was deleted without compilation or execution. The existing account is now restored through ordinary encrypted-key export/import in the Vive-capable browser. Signed read-only inspection of the current lobby (height 4) shows no physics_space/3, physics_agent/5 or physics_control/4 definitions; its committed external-predicate manifest contains only quod_agent_predicates. This exposes a production integration gap, beyond hardware acceptance: the normal lobby still uses observer movement. Commit validation deliberately rejects changes to the founding manifest, so enabling physics in this existing ontology cannot be a routine configuration edit. Integration choices and evidence are recorded in doc/evidence/player-movement/live-lobby-20261009/README.md. No domain writes or new accounts/ontologies were created. Ticket remains in progress.

2026-10-09 consolidation: keep this ticket open. The core collision/control foundation is committed with hot controls, but actual existing-lobby normal-view integration and physical Vive/WebXR movement acceptance are NOT complete. The undeployed external-predicate-selection experiment was surgically removed and archived; no lobby facts were changed. General existing-world integration is now tracked in [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27); optional native-client XR work is parked in [QUD.28](nimbalyst://QUD.28). One consolidation writer now owns integration; other sessions remain paused. No new server feature changes or deployment in consolidation. Evidence and full follow-up bodies: doc/evidence/workspace-consolidation-20261009/.

Step 1 (two-scope commit consolidation) is complete: inspection 465ad808a1165607be76145868a3e1528fc5c1a9, then failure handling + qualified browser assets a510f504bab1837f77dcfb27651891bc17e13521. All reconciled source/assets match the qualified bytes in both Git and the live checkout. Paused movement/WebXR evidence and other client work are preserved unchanged. No deployment or real-lobby/hardware acceptance was performed. This movement ticket remains open; general existing-world integration is tracked in QUD.27.

Deployment/refound boundary, 2026-10-10: the committed collision/control and failure-handling foundations are deployed in candidate release 0.7.256. Yan explicitly authorized a destructive ledger refound. The old eight candidate ledger volumes were deleted after a fresh founder started; the new root is `3F88D70B7714366EE11D38764231DD2F6EE8AAFC58EB8C0559146543E5280F26`, and the new lobby is `7B0DA9C7D3385065AD99A51B9987118FFA4C6DB837DA7211A924995206AD565A`. All 18 system ontologies were founded through existing governed actions and are ready on 8/8 healthy nodes. Evidence commit: `4ba646223870c4706f3c2ca0de4b84c76e4d2a92`; `doc/evidence/hot-controls/deployment-256-refound/`. This does not complete this item: the fresh lobby still needs the general governed physical-world/control integration tracked by QUD.27, followed by desktop and physical Vive collision-locomotion acceptance in that actual lobby. items.description:
## Goal and agreed architecture
Enable optional governed physics in existing ontology worlds and ordinary signed client views. The first acceptance target is Yan's actual current personal lobby, preserving its exact identity and history. This is a generic capability, not a lobby special case, and remains a prerequisite of [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26).

- Prolog decides whether a world is physical and whether simulation is enabled. [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33) supplies space and physical_space semantics; class membership alone does not load native predicates, allocate resources or authorize control. Ontology and space are independent classes. Text/3D ontology representation work in [QUD.32](nimbalyst://QUD.32)–[QUD.35](nimbalyst://QUD.35) is not a prerequisite for the entire physics slice.
- There is no backward-compatibility requirement: replace superseded paths, remove old/new branches and do not introduce a separate physics ontology merely to accommodate old code. Preserving this lobby's identity/history is a distinct requirement; no automatic refound, data wipe or history rewrite.
- Domain policy, actions, authorization and resource budgets stay in Prolog; external Erlang predicates are governed interfaces. One physics authority and one mutable owner for each truth; no second domain engine, private knowledge base or hidden fallback.

## Architecture gate
Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md, doc/multiwrite-architecture.md and existing ontology lifecycle/action/recovery owners. Trace existing composition and ordinary founding/bridge deployment before selecting the smallest missing capability. A linked normally founded physics scope is a candidate, not an accepted default; any boundary must be justified by governance/lifecycle, not backward compatibility. Do not silently resurrect the removed external_predicate_selection/reconcile_modules experiment.

Specify exact world/instance/body/agent references, capability authorization, compatible participating validators, concurrent-proof conflicts, rollback, recovery and withdrawal. Validator compatibility for the chosen deployment is not permission for permanent backward-compatibility code. Neither changing a package file nor declaring a class changes a retained founding manifest. If the selected design needs a new capability-evolution contract, bring that concrete gap to the applicable architecture/deployment gate rather than bypassing immutable provenance.

## Existing subscriptions, not another propagation path
A live collider defined in ontology A and consumed by subscribed physics authority P follows A's committed diffs through the existing subscription/verified-projection owners. An authorized edit must update the effective collider automatically; no manual re-adoption per edit, mirrored mutable collider store, polling loop, new diff broker or second synchronization protocol. Deliberately pinned reusable shape recipes are different from live referenced instances and must be explicit, never the default imposed to solve linkage.

Trace quod_runtime subscription handling and quod_foreign_log retained projections through the current local physics resource selector. Demonstrate any missing dependency-to-install wiring, extend that existing owner, and preserve subscribe-before-snapshot, exact source/body/structure revision fencing and installation notices. Recovery restores current verified state; correctness cannot depend on replaying or receiving every best-effort reaction. Related durable changes/receiver consequences form one existing atomic transaction; no post-commit repair workflow to reconnect artificially split writes.

## Physical definitions and normal views
- Author explicit physical geometry, agent/body binding and camera local position/orientation in Prolog. Support the native adapter's supported shapes through shared validation, not only a hardcoded box. Visual GLBs, picking bounds and Eidolon geometry are not collision authority. Preserve real openings, roof and console geometry.
- Future noncubic voxel/chunk geometry uses the same explicit geometry, resource-policy and revision contract; missing collision coverage is unknown, not empty. Terrain streaming is not part of this slice.
- Reuse the existing signed projection/control protocol in the ordinary view. Track visible-world, acting-agent, physics and actual authorization/geometry dependencies, including a disabled selection that later becomes enabled; current source/simulation-only subscriptions are not automatically sufficient.
- Preserve anchored instance/body identity, decorative marks, authored parents/attachment frames and camera transforms under one pose writer. Discovering physics only from a lobby rule is insufficient if the current lookup is in the acting agent's ontology.
- Distinguish observer travel, commanded body travel and tracked head movement. Unavailable physics must not silently switch a controlled body into observer travel.
- Distinguish nonphysical, disabled, denied, recovering and unavailable. Handle occupied spawn/reposition/teleport, collider edits/deletion, moving doors, revocation, reconnect and authority changes. Commit, installed state and mechanically fulfilled placement are separate; durable occupancy conclusions use existing authenticated observations, not live-query proof exemptions.
- Admission/withdrawal and any exclusive body assignment use the designated owners and existing atomic transitions. Resolve uncertain operations by original identity, never new submission. No generic inter-simulation handoff is assumed.

## Evidence and acceptance
October 9 signed lobby evidence and the removed experiment are historical: doc/evidence/player-movement/live-lobby-20261009/README.md and cleanup-20261009/README.md. A separately authorized October 10 refound is recorded under doc/evidence/hot-controls/deployment-256-refound/. Therefore establish the fresh signed personal-lobby identity/history baseline before acceptance; neither the old anchor nor the system lobby-vocabulary anchor identifies it automatically.

1. Generic production-owner tests across at least two world identities, including a non-lobby and a nonphysical case. Cover concurrent admission/edit/withdrawal, authorization, rollback, recovery and stale fences.
2. A real committed remote collider change reaches the subscribed installed physics owner through the existing path. Measure exact affected invalidation and unchanged repeat work: no history replay, projection/native geometry rebuild or storage write/sync caused by unchanged checks. Distinguish legitimate simulation stepping and real durable updates. Preserve current conservative world fencing/per-predicate OCC; do not claim row-level precision.
3. Real signed desktop collision acceptance in the normal view of the same existing lobby, preserving identity/history, console and openings. A fixture/simulated test world is not a substitute.
4. Physical Vive/WebXR landing, contact, tracking and comfort remain required separately by [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26). Durable real-lobby blocked/closed door acceptance is [QUD.36](nimbalyst://QUD.36); do not confuse moving-door collision coverage with that consequence acceptance.
5. Coordinate a single server writer and existing release authority. Client testing does not authorize broader runtime mutation or deployment.

The reviewed design is not implementation evidence. Keep this item open until all its own acceptance is verified.

items.title: Document Quod terminology for ontologies, instances, spaces and representations
items.description:
## Goal
Create a concise, source-checked terminology reference for this plan. Explain existing words rather than introducing another ontology taxonomy.

## Scope
- Define ontology (authoritative Prolog code/state, ACL and history boundary, also an instance of the ontology class), class, instance, space, physical space, agent, lens, encoding, Eidolon, mark, anchored reference, route/contact, body and physics authority.
- Distinguish subclass from instance membership; code/state ownership from spatial containment; ontology contents from a presentation of them; marks from body identity; source/interface inspection from permission to invoke or edit.
- Record Yan's choice: ontology and space are independent classes. Every accessible ontology may have 3D/text/policy representations; representation does not entail space membership. A space may be nonphysical; physical_space is a subtype of space. Physics enablement remains governed Prolog policy.
- Do not introduce “subject” as a new user-facing domain category. Existing source terms such as subject(Target, Entity) may be explained as current API syntax, not another kind of object.
- Link the reference from relevant architecture/GUI/physics documentation and reconcile contradictory terminology in the touched scope. Clearly distinguish implemented behavior from proposed refinements; do not rename APIs merely to satisfy the glossary.

## Acceptance
Definitions and examples map to actual class/instance/lens/Eidolon and owner code; one ontology shown in multiple views remains one authority/history. No new registry, universal metaclass system, runtime process or production semantics is introduced. Preserve frozen historical review evidence.

Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md and doc/multiwrite-architecture.md before implementation. Reuse existing Prolog policy/actions, lifecycle, recovery and authorized owner paths. No parallel domain engine, hidden fallback or backward-compatibility branch. Clean replacement does not authorize deployment, refounding or history deletion.

Related implementation: [QUD.32](nimbalyst://QUD.32) (ontology instances/ACLs), [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33) (spaces), [QUD.34](nimbalyst://QUD.34) (text), [QUD.35](nimbalyst://QUD.35) (3D workbench), [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27) (physics). This glossary is not a blanket blocker for those implementations.

items.description:
## Goal
Make each exact ontology available as an ordinary instance of the ontology class, reusing class/instance selection, lenses, encodings, Eidolons and marks. This refines the existing model, not a second ontology-object system.

## Scope
- Derive identity from existing namespace/genesis-anchor and lifecycle owners; expose authorized current source, explicitly declared interfaces, contacts/routes and ACLs through their real owners. A contact address is a route, not identity or a copied mutable directory field.
- Replace the ontology-specific selection/dispatch fork with the ordinary applicable-Eidolon path. Preserve exact target anchors through class diagrams, text/policy panels and 3D marks; a mark occurrence is not a new ontology. Do not assume every Eidolon is a code workspace.
- Preserve existing private ontology discovery boundaries; root's system catalogue is not a global list of personal ontologies.
- Expose ACL rules under the target's read policy, distinguishing source read, policy read, invocation, content edit and policy edit. Where effective permissions are displayed, make them bounded, context-relative advisory results; actual actions reauthorize against current state. Do not execute mutations as permission probes, invent a privileged arbitrary-goal oracle, or treat *_query/1 helpers as a universal public API catalogue.
- Location and state ownership remain independent under ACLs. Ontology and space are independent classes (Yan's explicit choice): a 3D representation does not imply isa(ontology, space), transfer ownership or enable physics.

## Acceptance
System and owned non-system ontologies use the same representation selection, with correct read-only/editable/denied behavior. Wrong anchors, private targets, stale permissions and unauthorized policy edits fail at the real owner. Authorized edits use existing transactions and exact-outcome handling. Multiple views stay on the same committed contents/history; unchanged inspection does no replay/rebuild/write/sync. Remove superseded ontology special dispatch, not retain an old/new compatibility path.

## Existing foundations
[QUD.20](nimbalyst://QUD.20) delivered system ACL enforcement and [QUD.24](nimbalyst://QUD.24) delivered complete-current-state inspection; keep them closed. Trace common_predicates.pl, quod_prolog_eidolons.pl, quod_prolog.pl, quod_lens.pl, client/src/world.js and ui/src/World.tsx. items.title: Define governed space and optional physical-space class semantics

blocks.title: Enable governed physics in existing ontology worlds and normal client views

items.description:
## Goal
Refine existing class vocabulary with space and its physical_space subtype. Spaces organize instances/information and may contain or depict classes and other spaces; they are not necessarily physical and are not synonymous with ontology code/state ownership.

## Agreed model
- Ontology and space are independent classes (Yan's explicit choice). An ontology can be represented/explored/edited in 3D without becoming a space. An instance may carry both roles only when explicitly authored with corresponding semantics.
- Trace isa/2, class-first instance_of/2 and actual inheritance/dispatch behavior before choosing predicate placement. Reuse existing ontology vocabulary/composition; do not introduce a generic container hierarchy or shadow object registry.
- Specify what containment asserts, which ontology owns each relation, and when it is purely organizational versus physical placement. A visual arrangement/lens layout does not change domain location unless an authorized action explicitly does so. Moving into a space does not move an instance's code, ACLs, identity or history.
- Class membership does not install native bridges, start actors, allocate resources or confer permissions. Prolog separately governs enablement, body admission, observation/control rights and resource policy. Several rooms may share one simulation authority; neither one ontology nor one simulator per room is a universal rule.

## Governed transitions
Admission checks both the instance owner's delegation and the space owner's policy. If exclusive physical placement is required, concurrent destinations must serialize the assignment at one designated owner, atomically with admission through existing multi-ontology transactions; unchanged read-only consent is insufficient. Specify authorized containment/physical edits, removal, withdrawal and revocation, including constraint/checkpoint cleanup, recovery and original-operation resolution. Do not implement a parallel ownership/handoff service or require transactions for purely local view layout and transient controls. Commit, runtime installation and physically fulfilled placement are distinct.

## Acceptance
Demonstrate a nonphysical information space and a physical space with non-lobby identities, authorized/denied containment, nested membership, competing exclusive admissions and withdrawal/recovery through production owners. Preserve one owner per mutable fact and existing identity/history. Prove class declaration alone allocates no simulation; automatic live collider updates remain the existing subscription mechanism, not containment-driven copying.

[QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27) owns physics integration and real-lobby acceptance. General transfer between independent simulations is outside the first slice; do not claim it works from atomic delete/add alone.

Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md and doc/multiwrite-architecture.md before implementation. Reuse existing Prolog policy/actions, lifecycle, recovery and authorized owner paths. No parallel domain engine, hidden fallback or backward-compatibility branch. Clean replacement does not authorize deployment, refounding or history deletion.

[QUD.31](nimbalyst://QUD.31) owns terminology; [QUD.32](nimbalyst://QUD.32) owns ontology-instance reflection. This task is a prerequisite of [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27), not a dependency on the full text/3D workbench.

items.title: Add a syntax-highlighted ontology text-editing Eidolon
items.description:
## Goal
Provide a dedicated ontology text-editing Eidolon with syntax highlighting for Quod Prolog, using the existing prolog_editor and authorized source/edit paths. This is an editable representation of the ontology, not a separate authoritative source document.

## Scope
- Present complete coherent current source by default, with optional selection delegated to existing lenses. Highlight facts, rules, variables, literals, comments and Quod-qualified calls correctly; support convenient indentation, search and readable editing/diagnostics within existing client controls.
- Keep local drafts and explicit change preview separate from committed state. Reuse existing signed submission, proof/accept cursor, conflict and unresolved-operation UI. A refresh or reconnect must not silently discard a draft, overwrite an intervening edit or resubmit an uncertain write.
- Extend the current predicate-scoped compiler only as needed for editing the displayed ontology text; multi-predicate changes that form one edit commit atomically against a coherent expected baseline. Preserve unselected/runtime-owned contents. Parser/resource rejection is explicit; do not split the edit to evade policy limits.
- Respect source-read/content-edit/policy-edit distinctions, private target ACLs and exact anchored identity. A reader gets a highlighted read-only view; selecting this Eidolon grants no new authority. Formatting/source-fidelity limitations of the current stored representation must be visible, not promised away.
- Reuse the ordinary ontology-instance Eidolon dispatch and existing controllers; do not build a second source engine, shadow KB or independent save protocol. No backward-compatibility shim.

## Acceptance
Edit facts and rules across multiple predicates on an authorized non-lobby ontology; verify the exact committed result through its owner and another representation. Cover parse error, stale concurrent edit, read-only user, wrong anchor, revocation, disconnect and lost reply with no uncertain resubmission. Verify complete-source reads and unchanged repeated operations reuse retained state. Desktop interaction is required; do not claim physical VR keyboard/comfort acceptance from a mockup.

[QUD.24](nimbalyst://QUD.24) is complete-current-state inspection, not completion of this editor. [QUD.20](nimbalyst://QUD.20) supplies ACL foundations; [QUD.25](nimbalyst://QUD.25) may supply shared controls without requiring its whole GUI milestone first.

Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md and doc/multiwrite-architecture.md before implementation. Reuse existing Prolog policy/actions, lifecycle, recovery and authorized owner paths. No parallel domain engine, hidden fallback or backward-compatibility branch. Clean replacement does not authorize deployment, refounding or history deletion.

items.title: Inspect and edit ontology contents in 3D through existing lenses and Eidolons
items.description:
## Goal
Let an authorized user see, interact with, edit and build ontology contents in 3D using existing lenses, encodings, Eidolons, marks and owner-authorized actions. Quod is not limited to walking through physical rooms.

## Scope
- Supply a bounded first 3D workbench for ontology contents: show classes, instances and selected relations; select exact anchored targets; inspect them and perform authorized creation/edit/deletion through existing action/editing owners. Define the first supported operations explicitly rather than promising a universal graphical Prolog editor.
- A class-diagram view, 3D workbench, text editor and ACL view are presentations of the same ontology. Switching or opening multiple representations does not clone its ontology, source or history. Ontologies themselves are ordinary class instances with Eidolons and marks.
- Reuse lens selection versus encoding/representation separation; do not impose an independent client filter or new presentation engine. Generalize the existing dispatcher as needed rather than treating all Eidolons as code forms.
- Distinguish presentation layout from actual domain edits. Moving a mark for readability does not move ownership or a physical body. Explicit domain edits use the target ACLs and expected state; correlated durable edits use existing atomic transactions.
- No automatic space/physical_space membership, simulation allocation or collision geometry from representation. Nonphysical ontologies must remain usable with no physics service.

## Acceptance
On a system read-only ontology and an owned non-lobby ontology, visualize coherent current content, inspect class/instance identity, create/edit/delete within granted policy and see the same committed result in the text view. Test denial, wrong anchor, concurrent edit, deleted targets, revocation and reconnect/uncertain outcomes. Local layout cannot mutate domain location. Repeated unchanged views do not replay history or rebuild retained state.

Reuse [QUD.25](nimbalyst://QUD.25)'s common GUI infrastructure where available; this ticket owns the ontology-editing application, not the general form/question lifecycle. The dedicated text Eidolon is a sibling consumer, not a second source of truth. Hardware VR interaction validation must be recorded separately from desktop/rendering checks.

Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md and doc/multiwrite-architecture.md before implementation. Reuse existing Prolog policy/actions, lifecycle, recovery and authorized owner paths. No parallel domain engine, hidden fallback or backward-compatibility branch. Clean replacement does not authorize deployment, refounding or history deletion.

Ordinary ontology-instance dispatch/ACL reflection: [QUD.32](nimbalyst://QUD.32). Highlighted text editing: [QUD.34](nimbalyst://QUD.34). Any actual space containment action uses [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33) rather than inferring location from mark layout.

items.description:
## Origin and goal
Preserve the physical-door acceptance explicitly deferred when Yan accepted [QUD.19](nimbalyst://QUD.19)'s visual-only lobby scope. The native/Prolog door foundation ([QUD.6](nimbalyst://QUD.6)) and pose transport ([QUD.7](nimbalyst://QUD.7)) are completed foundations, not proof of this actual-lobby interaction. [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27) first enables governed physics and the signed ordinary world view.

## Scope
In Yan's freshly identified current personal lobby, bind an explicit physical door/frame/hinge and obstacle to the existing authorized Eidolons/marks, preserving openings, roof, console and the lobby's exact identity/history. Expose close and the minimum authorized obstacle-edit/reset actions through existing GUI/action paths. Do not recreate the lobby or use a separate demonstration world as acceptance.

## Required acceptance
- Authorized close visibly moves the real door in the normal client. An obstacle stops it; the displayed stopped geometry agrees with the atomically committed blocked outcome/checkpoint. Clearing the obstacle then closing commits and displays closed, not merely an animation or native stop.
- Race obstacle edits, cancellation/replacement, duplicate/delayed samples, collider deletion/recreation and stale frames. No old sample completes a new request or resurrects a removed body.
- Resolve lost replies by the original operation. Reconnect, simulator restart and authority recovery restore committed stopped geometry/checkpoints without replaying completion reactions or silently substituting another world.
- Preserve the signed console, existing appearance/edition views and one pose source per body-bound occurrence. Unchanged reconciliation does no history replay, geometry rebuild or write/sync; measure real production-owner work.
- Record signed/browser evidence and applicable clean sequential gates with true exits. Coordinate a single server writer; deployment or broader runtime changes require the existing authority. Physical Vive contact/tracking/comfort acceptance remains [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26).

## Boundaries
This is level-based blocked/closed outcome integration, not [QUD.18](nimbalyst://QUD.18)'s general distinct-impact consequences, [QUD.9](nimbalyst://QUD.9)'s held objects or [QUD.10](nimbalyst://QUD.10)'s remote multi-viewer expansion. No scripted obstruction substitute, new transport/engine, live-query sealing exemption or hidden fallback.

Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md and doc/multiwrite-architecture.md before implementation. Reuse existing Prolog policy/actions, lifecycle, recovery and authorized owner paths. No parallel domain engine, hidden fallback or backward-compatibility branch. Clean replacement does not authorize deployment, refounding or history deletion.

Prerequisite integration: [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27); player/Vive acceptance: [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26); shared-physics umbrella: [QUD.3](nimbalyst://QUD.3).
